claim: Hot 100 and US Adult Contemporary peaks: Gypsys 1/6, Way of Love 7/2, Living in a House Divided 22/2, Don't Hide Your Love 46/19, Half-Breed 1/3, Dark Lady 1/3, Train of Thought 27/9, I Saw a Man 42/3, Pirate 93, Take Me Home 8/19 (US dance 2), Wasn't It Good 49, Hell on Wheels 59
Gypsys written by Bob Stone for Cher, produced by Snuff Garrett; Wrecking Crew backing; No. 1 Nov 6 1971 for two weeks; Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour debuted Aug 1971 (subagent extraction, spot-check)

Half-Breed: Mary Dean had Cher in mind; Garrett meant to quit working with Sonny and Cher after Sonny refused to let Cher record The Night the Lights Went Out in Georgia; No. 1 Oct 6 1973 for two weeks (subagent extraction, spot-check)
Dark Lady: John Durrill of the Ventures; week-long writing session with Garrett; lyrics by telegram while the Ventures toured Japan; No. 1 Mar 23 1974 for one week (subagent extraction, spot-check)
Half-Breed written by Mary Dean and Al Capps specifically for Cher
Dark Lady: Durrill played keyboards for the Ventures; two videos exist, a live performance on the Comedy Hour and an animated version; her last US No. 1 until Believe in 1998
Take Me Home by Michele Aller and Bob Esty, Esty produced; first big hit since Dark Lady
Take Me Home: Casablanca Records, released January 1979, lead single from her 15th album produced by Esty and Ron Dante; Ed Greene drums, Eddie Watkins Jr bass, Wah Wah Watson guitar; Hot 100 No. 8
I Saw a Man and He Danced with His Wife written by John Robert Durrill; Dark Lady written by Durrill

Gypsys was her first solo No. 1, performed on the Sonny and Cher show, about traveling Romani people; the show drew 30 million weekly viewers; Take Me Home a brief 1979 foray into disco she reportedly did not want to make
